newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower amid speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower amid speculative selling.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed sharply weaker in a speculative-led selloff that pressured the benchmark September contract to a new lifetime low, dealers said.
The contract slid to 73.50 cents before the selling dried up and trade buying emerged to buoy prices off the lows.
The market is expected to ease further on Thursday, with nearby support seen at 72.00 cents followed by 70.00 cents basis the September contract.
"This is not a good close and the technicals continue to point lower," a technical analyst said.
The September contract ended 0.85 cent weaker at 74.40 cents per lb, having ranged from 75.50 to its contract low of 73.50 cents. The rest of the board finished down 1.70 to 0.55.
An estimated 2,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Tuesday's official 3,130 lots.
Market sources blame recent weakness on both the technical and fundamental situations.
"We have slow sales, big supplies and even bigger crops forecast for next year," the analyst said. "It just keeps getting worse."
The U.S. Department of Agriculture has estimated the 1996/97 Florida crop at a record 224.2 million 90-lb boxes, and the current Brazilian crop at a record 18.3 million tonnes.
